protocol.question: Does a learned estimator correct per-ping sway phase on seabed patches better or faster than local GPGA and per-ping entropy?
protocol.data: PoSSM synthetic, noiseless; seabed-only ROIs away from inserted objects

scene_split.source: references/scene_split_v2.csv (fixed in v2, before this work)

protocol.training_corruption: phase only on clean ping stacks: theta_k = (4 pi / lambda) * (y / R) * d_k; d from the v3 sway model (navigation_path) with seeds >= 20000, RMS uniform 0-3 mm, 10% zero; lambda = c / 300 kHz, R from 6 m altitude
protocol.evaluation_corruption: geometric sway injection as v3: 2 mm RMS, IQ unchanged; validation seeds [7001, 7002]; test seeds [7101..7105]; clean control amount 0

methods.deep: learned estimator, weights chosen on validation only
methods.deep_entropy: per-ping entropy started from the deep estimate (single start)
methods.oracle: per-ping phase from the clean ping stack; upper bound, uses truth

protocol.gauge: constant and linear ping phase are not observable (absolute phase, along-track shift)
protocol.primary_metric: linear-phase registered complex NCC vs clean BP of the same ROI (best of 721 slopes in [-pi, pi])
protocol.selection: checkpoint, iterations and deep_entropy use chosen by validation median registered NCC; test run once
report: paired deep - entropy difference with patch-cluster bootstrap 95% CI (2000)
protocol.no_claim: no real-data or noisy-data performance; ROI centres are chosen from object-free seabed, not by a detector
